Switching vendors or adding a second source inside 14 days would introduce onboarding risk we cannot afford given the zero-buffer assembly line. Deferring is not viable because the contract does not auto-renew. Renewing as-is leaves the 18% cut unaddressed. The best single move is to negotiate_terms at renewal: memory_c4 already tells us that benchmarking against market rates moved the incumbent on both price and payment terms, and memory_c6 tells us that multi-year commitments unlocked volume pricing without narrowing service scope. Pulling memory_c6 lets me confirm the specifics of the multi-year volume pricing structure before walking into the negotiation, so I can anchor the ask correctly. This path keeps the incumbent relationship stable (no migration, no delivery interruption — consistent with memory_c1), captures the cost reduction finance requires, and avoids any onboarding risk to the already-tight assembly line.
